item.title: Product Hunt Daily | 2026-11-27
item.description:
1. Hub

Tagline: Run 100 Claude Code or Codex sessions like 5
Description: Open-source dispatcher for Claude Code and Codex sessions. Write a goal in your browser or Telegram, a coordinator hands it to agents, and only the decisions come back. Self-hosted, Apache-2.0, on your own Claude or ChatGPT subscription. One-line install. Experimental: agents run without permission prompts.
Website: open

2. QA.tech MCP

Tagline: Verify every change from your IDE with QA agents
Description: QA.tech MCP gives Claude Code, Cursor or Codex an external QA agent to check their work. It runs E2E tests on what each change does to your product and finds the bugs and edge cases your coding agent missed, so they get fixed before the PR goes to review. Stay in your IDE: QA.tech explores your app, writes the tests and runs them. Your coding agent reads the results and fixes what broke. Works with any MCP client. New to QA.tech? One prompt maps your app and kicks off your first test.
Website: open
Product Hunt: View on Product Hunt

3. ExtraOrbital

Tagline: ✦ Open bar databases, storage buckets & AI keys for agents
Description: Your app needs databases, storage, caching, AI keys, and more. That’s dozens of accounts, API keys, invoices, and backups to manage. Agents can’t stand it. They don’t even have access. You feel like their credentials go-fetch puppet. ExtraOrbital reads yourenv.example file and creates all these ressources for you. It’s a CLI, so your agents can use it. They don’t even need an account. You gain back control, increase security and manage everything in a central dashboard. Bye bye,env hell !
Website: open
Product Hunt: View on Product Hunt

Description: AI assistants now read websites for your buyers. Bifura fetches your page the way AI crawlers do, shows what they get and get wrong, and lets you test fixes in a sandbox before you ship. Free Agent readiness score in under a minute, no signup.

6. Doodle

Tagline: The stick figure on your taskbar that answers questions
Description: Doodle is a little AI companion that lives on your Windows taskbar. Ask it anything with Ctrl+Shift+Space, or dictate into any app. When it can’t do something, Doodle Evolution builds a bespoke plugin, shows you what it can reach, and waits for your OK.

7. Kagi Mail

Tagline: Private email that puts people who need you first
Description: Kagi Mail is a private email service designed to help you focus on what matters. Its intelligent inbox highlights people waiting for your reply, identifies emails that need action, and keeps newsletters and unwanted messages out of the way. Ask questions about your inbox, organize emails using natural-language rules, and use unlimited aliases and custom domains. No ads, no tracking, no profiling. Includes 50 GB storage and a built-in calendar, with open standards and no vendor lock-in.

8. Clary

Tagline: iOS notifications in sender’s own voice from WhatsApp & more
Description: Clary reads your iPhone notifications in the sender’s own voice, from WhatsApp, iMessage and more. It uses voice cloning: each person records 20 seconds once, from a link, and agrees first, then Clary makes their voice on your iPhone. Tap a message to hear it in their voice, so you feel closer to your people. It also keeps your notifications as a history on your iPhone, sorted Gmail-style into Messages, Updates and Promotions. Free: history, sorting and 2 plays. Needs iPhone 15 Pro+ and iOS 27.

9. Monton

Tagline: AI agents that do your agency’s busywork
Description: Monton is agency management software with AI agents built in. Agents watch budgets, chase overdue invoices, write client reports and remind people about missing hours, on your real hours, staffing, billing and CRM data. Pick one of 18 templates or describe it in a chat. Every email waits for your approval. AI is included in every paid plan: no credits, no per-seat pricing. Free up to 5 people.

10. DeskFleet

Tagline: Run coding agents together across your team’s machines
Description: DeskFleet gives your team a shared session with the coding agents you already use. Run Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor where your code lives. A teammate can join from their laptop, review the diff, approve the next command, or take control of the remote desktop. Your tools and agent credentials stay on the machine doing the work.
